title: The Covenant of Salt
subtitle: Prophetic Actions That Destroy Principalities and Powers
service_date: Saturday Evening Deliverance Service · Mother's Day Weekend
main_scripture_text: Ought ye not to know that the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
short_description: A biblical deliverance teaching by Pastor Kiky Ocansey on the covenant of salt and the power of prophetic action. Pastor Kiky opens 2 Chronicles 13:5, 1 Chronicles 18:12 and 2 Kings 2:19-22 to show that God has always joined His word to obedient action, and she gives the seven-day prophetic direction the room received: pray over salt water, wash your face, sprinkle salt through your home, and stand on the covenant of salt against every principality and power hovering over your life and your destiny.
tagline: Luke 1:37 — For with God nothing shall be impossible.
summary: In this closing segment of a Saturday-evening deliverance service, Pastor Kiky Ocansey answered a simple question from the room — what is the salt water for? — and turned it into a full teaching on prophetic action. She laid three scriptures on the table: 2 Chronicles 13:5, where God gave David dominion for ever by a covenant of salt; 1 Chronicles 18:12, where eighteen thousand enemies fell in the valley of salt; and 2 Kings 2:19-22, where Elisha cast salt into a poisoned spring and God said, I have healed these waters. From those verses she taught that salt in scripture carries two meanings — preservation, and the destruction of principalities and powers — and that believers may stand on the covenant of salt in warfare. She then grounded the whole practice in the wider biblical pattern of prophetic action: Moses lifting the rod, Joshua compassing Jericho, and Jesus Himself making clay of the spittle and sending the blind man to wash. Her reasoning for why God uses earthly elements is a creation argument — God formed man of the dust of the ground, so if something is wrong with man, He will use the earth to correct it — always under one strict rule: it must stand with the scripture. She gave the room a seven-day direction (pray over salt water and wash the face daily, with the prayer points posted on the WhatsApp platform), taught how to walk a house with salt and evict every principality through the door in Jesus' name, explained that deliverance may leave loudly or very quietly and that both are real, and closed by sealing every deliverance with the blood of Jesus — with the pastoral reminder that even five honest minutes of prayer is received by God.
key_lessons: Faith without works is dead. Prayer and obedient action together bring the breakthrough (James 2:26).
Some attacks did not come by evil speaking alone — they came by actions. So the answer includes obedient action too.
God has always joined His word to a physical act: the rod, the march, the clay, the new cruse of salt.
The covenant of salt is a perpetual and unbreakable agreement. By it, no enemy shall prevail in your territory (2 Chronicles 13:5).
Salt signifies preservation and the destruction of principalities and powers.
God healed the waters — the salt did not. All power belongs to the Lord and to the finished work of Christ.
Nothing is used in prayer unless it stands with the scripture.
Matthew 5:13 — you are the salt. Guard your savour: repent and forgive before you fight.
Deliverance may leave loudly or very quietly. Everybody has a way of being delivered.
Seal every deliverance with the blood of Jesus, and keep a pure heart afterwards.
Even five minutes of honest love toward God is received by Him.

modules.title: Faith Without Works Is Dead
modules.quote: There is a teaching that we did in this room called faith without works is dead. And I give them the understanding of how powerful their works and their prayers combined together will give them a breakthrough.

levels.simple: Praying is talking to God. Works means doing what God tells you to do. God wants both. If you only talk and never do, nothing moves.
levels.teen: You can pray about the same thing for months and still feel stuck. Pastor Kiky is saying that is often because prayer was only half of the assignment. God gives an instruction with the prayer, and the instruction has to be carried out. Faith plus obedience is what breaks the thing.
levels.adult: Pastor Kiky says plainly: sometimes you are praying and praying and praying without works, and then the problems in your life keep on moving forward and not breaking. James does not devalue faith — he says works complete it. By works was faith made perfect. So when prayer has been offered and nothing has shifted, the honest question is not whether God heard, but whether there was an assigned action left undone.
levels.deeper: James 2 is not setting works against faith; it is setting living faith against dead faith. Even the devils believe, and tremble (James 2:19) — so belief alone is not the dividing line. Abraham's faith was reckoned to him as righteousness, and that same faith moved him to the altar. Pastor Kiky applies this to warfare: she notes that some attacks did not come by evil speaking alone — they came by actions as well. Where the enemy has used actions to establish a plague, the believer's answer includes obedient action, not only speech. This is why the room is taught prophetic actions every time it prays.

modules.keypoint: Some attacks in your life did not come by evil speaking alone. They came by actions. So your deliverance also includes obedient action, not only prayer.

modules.title: What Is a Prophetic Action?
modules.eyebrow: God has always joined His word to an act
modules.quote: They got to the Red Sea. They were looking at the sea. They didn't know what to do. But the Lord said to Moses, you've got the rod. Lift up the rod, and that would open the sea. You don't just have to stand there. Moses was praying, and calling upon the name of the Lord. But the Lord says, Moses, there is an action you need to do to open the sea.

levels.simple: A prophetic action is something God tells you to do with your body or with something you can hold. Moses lifted a stick. Israel marched around a city. God did the miracle after they obeyed.
levels.teen: Think of it as God saying: do this one physical thing, and I will move. Moses had a rod — not a weapon, just a stick. Israel had to walk laps around a wall for seven days, which must have looked ridiculous. But the action was the doorway for the power.
levels.adult: A prophetic action is a physical act of obedience that God attaches to His promise. At the Red Sea, Moses was already praying — God's response was Wherefore criest thou unto me? Lift thou up thy rod. At Jericho, God said See, I have given into thine hand Jericho — the victory was already granted — and yet Israel still had to compass the city, march seven days, blow the trumpets, and shout. Pastor Kiky's summary: surround it, go around it seven times, do some actions and the walls will fall. Sometimes without your actions, your deliverance will not come to pass.
levels.deeper: Note the theology carefully. In neither case does the action produce the power. The sea was divided by the Lord; the wall of Jericho fell because God had already given the city. The action is the appointed point of contact for faith — the place where believing becomes visible. That is why God specifies the details: the rod, the seven priests, the rams' horns, the seventh day, the seven circuits, the great shout. Obedience in the details is the substance of the faith. Remove the action and you have sentiment; remove the God who commanded it and you have superstition. Prophetic action lives between those two errors, and it is always grounded in a word God actually spoke.

modules.keypoint: Sometimes without your actions, your deliverance will not come to pass. Get to know your actions.

modules.title: Jesus Himself Did Prophetic Actions
modules.quote: Jesus always do prophetic actions. He wanted the blind man to see, right? So he spits on the ground and he made like a clay of the spittle. And then he placed it on the blind man's eye and then he told the blind man to go and wash his face in the water. And what happened? He was able to see.

levels.simple: Jesus could have just said the word. Instead He spat on the ground, made clay, put it on the blind man's eyes, and told him to go and wash. The man obeyed, and then he could see.
levels.teen: This is the cleanest proof that prophetic action is not weird or unbiblical. Jesus — who had all authority — chose to use dirt and spit and a walk to a pool. Nothing in that mixture had power. The power was in Christ. The clay and the walk were the obedience.
levels.adult: John 9 is Pastor Kiky's anchor example. Jesus did not need materials, and He did not need the man to walk anywhere. Yet He deliberately used the ground, and He deliberately gave the man something to do: Go, wash in the pool of Siloam. The healing arrived on the far side of obedience — he went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing. If the sinless Son of God attached an action to a miracle, no believer should despise a scriptural instruction as beneath them.
levels.deeper: Siloam means Sent, as John pauses to tell us — which is the whole gospel in a place name: the Sent One heals through the sent man. Notice also the order of the elements. Christ's own act of grace comes first (He anointed the eyes); the man's obedience comes second (he washed). Prophetic action never initiates the mercy — it responds to it. And the material Jesus chose was the same material man was made from, which is exactly the point Pastor Kiky draws out in the next module.

modules.keypoint: The blind man was not healed by clay. He was healed by Christ — and the healing met him inside his obedience.

modules.title: Why God Uses the Earth
modules.quote: The word of the Lord says thus we are and thus we will go. So Jesus took the earth knowing that is the part of the earth — God used the earth to make man, so if there is something wrong with man I will use the earth to correct it.

levels.simple: God made your body out of the ground. So when something is wrong with your body, God can use things from the ground — like salt, oil, or water — to help fix it.
levels.teen: God is not embarrassed by physical stuff. He made you out of physical stuff. That is why the Bible is full of oil, water, bread, wine and salt. They are not magic ingredients; they are earth-things God chose to attach His word to.
levels.adult: Pastor Kiky reasons from creation. God formed man of the dust of the ground (Genesis 2:7), and dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return (Genesis 3:19). Because the body came out of the earth, God is willing to use the earth in correcting the body. She then points to 1 John 5:8 — there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood. In the room she names the blood, the water, and the oil of the Spirit, and adds the fragrance of the Lord. Her governing rule is strict: anything you use must stand with the scripture.
levels.deeper: This is a creation-and-incarnation argument. The God who made matter is not a God who despises matter — He formed Adam from soil, He was born in a body, He used bread and a cup to memorialize His death, and He will raise the physical dead. So the use of a physical element in prayer is not paganism when three conditions hold: (1) the element is one God Himself named in scripture, (2) the word spoken over it is a scripture God actually wrote, and (3) all the power is credited to Christ's finished work and none to the substance. Remove any of the three and it collapses into superstition. Pastor Kiky's rule — anything that stands with the scripture — is exactly the safeguard that keeps prophetic action inside Christian ground.

modules.keypoint: God made man from the earth, so He is willing to use the earth to correct man. But nothing is used unless it stands on a scripture.

modules.title: The Covenant of Salt
modules.quote: In 2nd Chronicles chapter 13 verse 5 God established an everlasting, permanent covenant with David and his descendants to rule over Israel. So the phrase covenant of salt signifies a perpetual and unbreakable covenant, symbolized by the use of salt in sacrifice. The covenant of salt, beloved, indicates a lasting and unbreakable agreement with the Lord your God in the mighty name of Jesus — meaning that by His covenant and agreement, no enemy will or shall prevail in your territory in the mighty name of Jesus.

levels.simple: A covenant is a promise that cannot be broken. God called His promise to David a covenant of salt because salt does not spoil. God's promise to you does not spoil either.
levels.teen: Salt was the ancient world's way of saying this will not go off. Meat with salt lasts. So when God calls His agreement a covenant of salt, He is saying: this deal has no expiry date. That is the ground you stand on when you fight.
levels.adult: Ought ye not to know that the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt? Pastor Kiky lifts two words out of that verse: for ever, and covenant. God gave David dominion, and He sealed it in permanence. Her application is direct: as God gave dominion to David by the covenant of salt, He will give us dominion over our enemies, over the wicked in our life and in our destiny, by the power of the Holy Ghost. By His covenant no enemy shall prevail in your territory.
levels.deeper: The phrase covenant of salt appears three times in scripture: Leviticus 2:13, Numbers 18:19, and 2 Chronicles 13:5. In Leviticus, salt is required in every offering — the salt of the covenant of thy God was not to be lacking. In Numbers, the priestly portion is given by a covenant of salt for ever. In 2 Chronicles, Abijah invokes it against Israel's rebellion to argue that David's throne is legally unassailable. So the covenant of salt is a legal argument about permanence: it is what you cite when someone contests what God has already settled. For the believer that permanence is now located in Christ, the Son of David, whose kingdom has no end. When Pastor Kiky says we stand on that covenant of salt, she is standing on an unbreakable verdict, not on a mineral.

modules.keypoint: The covenant of salt means a perpetual, unbreakable agreement. By that covenant, no enemy shall prevail in your territory.

modules.title: The Valley of Salt
modules.eyebrow: Salt as a place of victory
modules.quote: 1st Chronicles chapter 18 verse 12 — the word of the Lord says, moreover Abishai the son of Zeruiah slew of the Edomites in the valley of salt eighteen thousand. Beloved, we use the salt for our warfare in the name of Jesus.

levels.simple: In the Bible there was a place called the valley of salt. God's people won a huge battle there. Salt is not just for food. It is also connected to winning.
levels.teen: Eighteen thousand enemies fell in a place literally named the valley of salt. Most people only know the one verse about being the salt of the earth. Pastor Kiky is showing that scripture connects salt to battle and victory too.
levels.adult: Abishai the son of Zeruiah slew of the Edomites in the valley of salt eighteen thousand. Pastor Kiky uses this to establish that salt appears in scripture at the site of decisive victory over an enemy nation. In the room, one believer said the only salt verse they knew was Matthew 5:13 — ye are the salt of the earth. Pastor Kiky's reply was to hand over the wider witness: 2 Chronicles 13:5, 1 Chronicles 18:12, and 2 Kings 2:19-22. Her conclusion: we use the salt for our warfare, and we stand on these scriptures, that by the power of the Holy Ghost He will give us dominion over our enemies.
levels.deeper: Two clarifications keep this sound. First, the valley of salt is a geographical location south of the Dead Sea, not a ritual instrument — the text is reporting a battlefield, and Pastor Kiky uses it typologically, as a picture of salt-ground being victory-ground. Second, Matthew 5:13 gives the New Testament weight: the believer himself is the salt. Christ's people are the preserving presence in a decaying world, and salt that has lost its savour is good for nothing. So the warfare application must never become external only. The salt in the bowl means nothing if the salt in the life has lost its savour — which is exactly why the standard deliverance flow puts confession of sins and forgiveness before any prayer of warfare.

modules.keypoint: Salt-ground is victory-ground. But Matthew 5:13 says you are the salt — so guard your savour before you fight.

modules.title: Elisha and the Healed Waters
modules.quote: As he placed the salt in the water, the water became what? Healed. He says, never again, because of this salt placed in this water, never again would this water, would this land, be unproductive. It became productive after the salt. You understand?

levels.simple: A city had bad water and nothing would grow. Elisha put salt in a new bowl, threw it in the spring, and said God has healed this water. The water became good and stayed good.
levels.teen: The city looked great — the situation of this city is pleasant — but the water was bad, so nothing produced. That is a picture of a life that looks fine on the outside and produces nothing. God healed the source, not the scenery.
levels.adult: Pastor Kiky reads the passage and then makes the application personal: sometimes when you are using this salt, just imagine — this city or this land is like your vessel, your body. There is something wrong with your body, so it is being unproductive; it is not acting the way it is supposed to act, not functioning the way it is supposed to function. So you get the bowl, and you put salt in water, and as you pray and drink it you say: whatever is causing my vessel, my body, not to be productive, to be weak, to be sick, whatever is plaguing my system, whatever is tormenting my mind — by the power of the Holy Ghost, as I drink this salt water in the name of Jesus, may it become productive again, may I receive healing again, may I receive the power of the Lord, may I receive the strength of the Lord. She then stands on the verse: He said, I have healed this water; there shall not be from thence any more death or barren land. No death will come to my life. No weakness will come to my life.
levels.deeper: The exegetical anchor is verse 21: Thus saith the Lord, I have healed these waters. The healing is credited to the Lord's word, announced by the prophet, at the moment of the obedient act. The salt is not a purifying agent — chemically, salt would make a bad spring worse. That impossibility is the point: the sign is deliberately powerless so that the glory is unambiguous. Note also verse 20 — a new cruse. God specified an unused vessel; even the container was set apart. And note the durability in verse 22: so the waters were healed unto this day. Pastor Kiky's typological reading (city as vessel, spring as source, barrenness as unfruitfulness) is a devotional application, not a claim that the text is about a human body — and she keeps the healing where the text puts it, in the mouth of the Lord.

modules.keypoint: God healed the source, and the healing lasted. Salt did not clean the spring — the word of the Lord did.

levels.simple: For seven days: put salt in water, pray over it, and wash your face with it. Pray the prayer points from the WhatsApp platform while you do it. Do it every day for the whole seven days.
levels.teen: It is a seven-day assignment, not a one-off. Salt in water, prayer over the water, wash the face, pray the prayer points. The consistency is part of the obedience — Naaman had to dip seven times, not once.
levels.adult: The direction as Pastor Kiky gave it: on the Wednesday service the room prayed with salt water and destroyed every enchantment, every curse, every divination, every spell over their lives and over their destiny. In this Saturday service she called for a check-in and told the room the direction and the prayer would be reposted so anyone who missed it could begin. Any edible salt the believer already has is acceptable — members in the room used Dead Sea salt and Himalayan salt, and Pastor Kiky's answer was simply to bring it and begin.

Second, if a day is missed, there is no penalty and no restart ritual — you simply continue. Nothing in Christian obedience operates on the logic of a broken spell. The water is water; Christ is the deliverer.

modules.title: Salt Around Your House
modules.quote: Take the salt, walk around your house. You said, this salt is for preservation, destruction of principalities and powers. As I sprinkle this salt around my house, I destroy every principality, every power hovering around my household. And then you open your door, and then you begin to cast it out — say, out of here, in the name of Jesus — and then you shut the door.

levels.simple: Walk around your house with salt. Pray out loud. Tell any evil spirit to leave in the name of Jesus. Open the door, send it out, then shut the door.
levels.teen: This is an eviction, not a decoration. You are speaking to something, telling it that it has no legal right to be in your home, and putting it out through the door in Jesus' name. The salt marks the boundary you are declaring.
levels.adult: Pastor Kiky gives the words as well as the action: this is my house, I pay the rent over here, you have no right to be here in the mighty name of Jesus, come out by the power of the Holy Ghost. She notes that where believers have been hearing knocking or noises in the house, this is one of the actions she teaches — and she adds that you can do the same with the blood of Jesus, or you can anoint your home. The salt is one option among several; the constant is speaking with authority in the name of Jesus. She closes it in prayer: any spirit hovering around my home, any spirit, principalities, powers, I rebuke you now, out of my house, in the mighty name of Jesus.
levels.deeper: Notice the legal logic, which is thoroughly biblical: I pay the rent over here, you have no right to be here. Deliverance addresses rights and grounds, not atmospheres — and the believer's right over his own dwelling is real, derived from Christ's authority (Luke 10:19; Matthew 18:18). Two guardrails. First, Pastor Kiky explicitly offers alternatives — salt, the blood of Jesus, or anointing the home — which proves the substance is not the agent. Second, a house cannot be held clean while sin, unforgiveness, or occult objects remain in it; eviction without repentance is Matthew 12:44, an empty house swept and garnished. Fill the house afterwards with worship, the word, and prayer.

modules.title: How Deliverance Leaves the Body
modules.quote: Everybody has a way of being delivered. Some deliverance, it goes very quietly — you don't even feel like nothing is left, but something is left. And some comes out because when the enemy is attacking you, it comes through air or liquid, by the spirit or by liquid, by physical things. So when he's leaving, he leaves by air or liquid, and he leaves by every opening of the body.

levels.simple: Not everybody feels the same thing when God sets them free. Some people feel nothing at all, and they are still free. Do not measure your deliverance by your feelings.
levels.teen: Some people cry, some yawn or burp, some feel nothing. Pastor Kiky's point is that everybody has a way of being delivered. If you felt nothing, that does not mean nothing happened — she says plainly, you don't even feel like nothing is left, but something is left.
levels.adult: Pastor Kiky teaches that what came in by air or liquid also leaves by air or liquid, and that it leaves by every opening of the body — by vomiting, by coughing or pulling it out, by burping, by crying. She is equally clear that some deliverance goes very quietly. The pastoral value of this teaching is that it removes both fear and comparison: a loud manifestation is not proof of greater bondage, and a silent one is not proof of no deliverance. Her closing counsel is about continuation — anytime they come, let it go by the power of the Holy Ghost, and let the Holy Spirit continue to fight for you and continue to deliver you.
levels.deeper: Scripture records that spirits departed with visible commotion — the unclean spirit cried with a loud voice and came out (Mark 1:26); the boy was torn and lay as one dead (Mark 9:26) — and also that deliverance came with no described physical event at all (Matthew 8:16; Matthew 15:28). Both are in the text, which is precisely Pastor Kiky's point. Two safeguards must be stated. First, no manifestation is ever the evidence of salvation or of freedom; the fruit that follows is (Matthew 7:20). Second, a bodily symptom must never be assumed to be spiritual by default. The L137 aftercare standard is explicit: seek qualified pastoral and medical support when appropriate. Persistent, severe or frightening physical symptoms should be seen by a doctor. Believing God and seeing a physician are not rivals.

modules.keypoint: Some deliverance is loud and some is silent. Both are real. Measure your freedom by fruit and by the word, never by feeling.

modules.title: Sealing, a Pure Heart, and Five Minutes
modules.quote: Sometimes even with prayer, the Lord is not asking you to pray for one hour, two hours — no. Even if it's for five minutes, and you can just say, Lord, I love You, I love You so much, and thank You for Your protection — even that alone, He receives.

levels.simple: After God sets you free, keep close to Him. You do not need to pray for hours. Five minutes of loving God is received by Him.
levels.teen: Aftercare is the part people skip. Pastor Kiky's version is refreshingly un-heavy: keep your heart pure, stay close to God, and if you cannot pray at length, listen to the word, listen to preaching, listen to things that make you feel light. Five honest minutes counts.
levels.adult: Pastor Kiky seals every deliverance with the blood of Jesus and prays that whatever left the body would not return. Then she gives the continuation counsel: keep your heart pure, continue to pray, and stay close to Him. She makes room for low seasons — sometimes you do not feel like praying out, so listen to the word, listen to preaching, listen to things that will make you feel light around you; continue to engage with the presence of the Lord. And she lowers the bar deliberately: even five minutes of Lord, I love You, thank You for Your protection, He receives. The room also decreed Ezekiel 21:27 over unexplainable setbacks, hindrances and delays, and the sealing prayer stood on Isaiah 54:17 — no weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper.
levels.deeper: This is the doctrine of perseverance handled pastorally. The sealing is not a second work added to Christ's; it is the appropriation of what His blood already secured (Hebrews 9:14; Revelation 12:11). The warning against the returning spirit is Christ's own (Matthew 12:43-45) and the remedy is occupancy — a heart filled with the word, worship, fellowship, and a renewed mind (Romans 12:2). Pastor Kiky's five-minute counsel guards against the real danger of legalistic aftercare, where a delivered believer replaces bondage to fear with bondage to a prayer quota. Isaiah 54:17 grounds the confidence: righteousness is of me, saith the Lord — the heritage is given, not earned. And the ministry's anchor closes it: for with God nothing shall be impossible.

characters: David
2 Chronicles 13:5; 2 Samuel 7:12-16
The shepherd king to whom God gave the kingdom over Israel for ever by a covenant of salt. David is the proof that God's grants are permanent, not probationary.
Your covenant with God does not expire. Fight from a settled verdict, not for one.
Abijah
2 Chronicles 13:4-12
King of Judah, David's descendant, who stood on Mount Zemaraim and reminded rebellious Israel of the covenant of salt. He cited the covenant as a legal argument in the middle of a war.
In warfare, cite the covenant. Remind the enemy of what God has already settled.
Abishai son of Zeruiah
1 Chronicles 18:12; 2 Samuel 23:18
One of David's mighty men, brother of Joab. He struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the valley of salt — a decisive victory in a salt place.
Salt-ground became victory-ground. The place of your bitterest battle can become the place of your greatest triumph.
Elisha

The prophet who asked for a new cruse with salt in it, cast it into the poisoned spring, and declared: Thus saith the Lord, I have healed these waters. He is also the prophet who sent Naaman to dip seven times in Jordan.
Prophetic instructions are often small, ordinary and repeatable — and God attaches His healing word to them.
Naaman
2 Kings 5:1-14
The Syrian commander who was offended by a small instruction, then obeyed it and dipped seven times in Jordan. His flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child.
Do not despise a simple instruction. If the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it?
Moses
Exodus 14:15-16
At the Red Sea Moses was crying out to God. God's reply was not more prayer but action: lift thou up thy rod, and stretch out thine hand over the sea.
There is a moment when the next step of faith is not another prayer but the act God already commanded.
Joshua
Joshua 6:2-5
Given a city that was already his — See, I have given into thine hand Jericho — and still required to march, blow trumpets, and shout before the wall fell flat.
A given victory still requires obedient action. Surround it, go around it seven times, and the walls will fall.
The man born blind
John 9:1-7
Jesus spat on the ground, made clay of the spittle, anointed his eyes and sent him to wash in the pool of Siloam. He went, washed, and came seeing.
The miracle met him inside his obedience. Christ healed him — the clay and the walk were the faith.
Abraham
James 2:21-23; Genesis 22
Cited by James as the man whose faith was made perfect by works when he offered Isaac upon the altar, and who was called the Friend of God.
Works do not replace faith — they complete it. Faith that obeys is living faith.
Rahab
James 2:25; Joshua 2
Named alongside Abraham by James: justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out another way.
Faith acted on at personal risk is the faith God honours — whatever your past.
Adam
Genesis 2:7; Genesis 3:19
Formed of the dust of the ground, with the breath of life breathed into his nostrils. Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
God made the body from the earth, so He is willing to use the earth to correct the body — always by His word, never by the substance.

given: Put salt in water, pray over it, and wash your face with the salt water. Do this every day for seven days, praying the prayer points posted on the WhatsApp platform. The room first prayed with the salt together and destroyed every enchantment, every curse, every divination and every spell over their lives and their destinies.

Take the salt and walk around your house. Say: this salt is for preservation and the destruction of principalities and powers. As I sprinkle this salt around my house, I destroy every principality and every power hovering around my household. Then open your door, cast them out — out of here, in the name of Jesus — and shut the door. Pastor Kiky notes you may do the same with the blood of Jesus, or anoint your home.
Salt water for an unproductive body

Standing on 2 Kings 2:19-22, put salt in water and pray: whatever is causing my vessel, my body, not to be productive, to be weak, to be sick; whatever is plaguing my system, whatever is tormenting my mind — by the power of the Holy Ghost, as I drink this salt water in the name of Jesus, may it become productive again, may I receive healing again, may I receive the power and the strength of the Lord.

Any edible salt you already have is acceptable. Members in the room used Dead Sea salt and Himalayan salt, and Pastor Kiky's answer was simply to bring it and begin. Elisha's pattern also honours the vessel — bring me a new cruse (2 Kings 2:20) — so use a clean bowl.

safeguards: The element must be named in scripture
Salt (2 Chronicles 13:5; 2 Kings 2:20), water and oil and blood (1 John 5:8), the earth itself (Genesis 2:7; John 9:6). Pastor Kiky's rule: anything that stands with the scripture.
The word spoken must be a scripture God actually wrote
Never invent a verse. Never invent a doctrine. The authority is in the word, and the word is quoted, not improvised.
All the power belongs to Jesus Christ

2 Kings 2:21 credits the healing to the Lord alone: Thus saith the Lord, I have healed these waters. Salt would chemically make a bad spring worse — the sign is deliberately powerless so the glory is unambiguous.
The substance is never the agent
Pastor Kiky offers alternatives in the same breath — salt, the blood of Jesus, or anointing the home. Interchangeable signs prove the object is not the power.
The heart comes before the action
Matthew 5:13 — you are the salt. The standard deliverance flow puts praise, thanksgiving, confession of sins and forgiveness before any warfare.
Nothing builds up over seven days. Naaman dipped seven times according to the saying of the man of God (2 Kings 5:14) — the cleansing came on God's word, not on the river.
Never sourced from occult or New Age practice
L137 draws only on scripture and reputable Christian references. No divination, no charms, no spells, no astrology — the service itself renounces every enchantment, curse, divination and spell.
Medical care is not a lack of faith
The L137 aftercare standard: seek qualified pastoral and medical support when appropriate. Persistent or severe physical symptoms should be seen by a doctor.
